transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

This sounds like the hob's safety system kicking in because it thinks it is overheating. On induction hobs, this usually happens if the cooling fan isn't running properly, the vents are blocked by nearby cabinetry, or a temperature sensor has failed. To narrow this down: first, is there any error code (like E1 or similar) shown on the display when it cuts out? Second, please check that the ventilation slots underneath or around the hob aren't blocked by cupboards or stored items.
a code flashes sometimes but too quick to read. not pulling anything out to check vents tho. a new drawer unit went in under it last month, cuts out started after that

That timeline suggests the new cabinetry is blocking the hob’s cooling vents. Induction hobs generate significant heat in their control electronics, which must be dissipated by a fan drawing air through those slots; if the airflow is restricted, the unit will shut down to prevent damage after 5-10 minutes of high load. Please check the gap underneath and ensure no items are blocking the intake or exhaust vents. If you can confirm there is adequate clearance and it still cuts out, we’ll need to investigate the internal cooling fan or sensors.
already said im not pulling the drawer out or checking under it. so what now? fan roars before it cuts out btw

The roaring noise you hear right before it cuts out is the cooling fan running at maximum speed to try and prevent overheating. Since this started after new drawers were fitted underneath, the most likely cause is that the hob’s internal airflow is blocked by the cabinetry, forcing the fan to work so hard it triggers a safety shutdown. If there is no visible gap between the bottom of your drawer unit and the hob frame, or if the vents are covered, this is an installation issue that needs correcting (you may need to raise the hob or trim the cabinet). However, if you can confirm there is at least 2-3cm of clear space around all vents and it still does this, the fan itself has likely failed and will need replacing by a qualified engineer.
